standard.title: Articles with Days & Time of Day
standard.explanation: In French, days of the week are used with the definite article 'le' when describing a habit or something that repeats. Use 'le lundi' to mean 'on Mondays' (every Monday). Without the article, 'lundi' refers to a specific upcoming Monday. Time of day expressions like 'le matin' (in the morning), 'l'après-midi' (in the afternoon), 'le soir' (in the evening), and 'la nuit' (at night) also use articles when referring to general times. Example: 'Le lundi matin, j'ai cours.' means 'On Monday mornings, I have class.'

advanced.title: Articles with Days & Time of Day — le lundi vs lundi, Time Expressions & Nuances
advanced.explanation: French distinguishes between habitual and specific uses of days of the week. 'Le lundi' means 'on Mondays' (every Monday, a habit), while 'lundi' or 'ce lundi' refers to a specific Monday. Similarly, time expressions like 'le matin,' 'l'après-midi,' 'le soir,' and 'la nuit' take articles when used generically. However, in fixed expressions like 'c'est lundi' (it is Monday) or 'c'est le matin' (it is morning), the article may be optional. Adverbial time phrases like 'ce matin' (this morning) and 'cet après-midi' (this afternoon) use 'ce' (demonstrative) instead of the article. Temporal contexts matter: 'Le jeudi, je suis libre' (on Thursdays I am free) vs. 'Jeudi, je ne peux pas' (this Thursday I cannot).

standard.scenario: Your friend asks you what you do each day of the week. Describe your typical week, mentioning at least three different days and the activities you do.
standard.modelAnswer: Le lundi, je vais à l'école. Mardi, j'aime jouer au foot. Le mercredi, je travaille l'après-midi. Samedi, je reste à la maison et je regarde la télévision. Dimanche, ma famille se réunit pour le dîner.
standard.modelAnswerExplanation: This answer uses 'le' + day name to describe habitual activities and uses present-tense verbs with first-person singular forms.
standard.tip: Remember: use 'le' + day name when talking about what you typically do on that day. 'Le lundi, je...' = 'On Mondays, I...'

advanced.scenario: Your French colleague asks you to describe your weekly schedule in detail. Include specific times, different activities at different times of day, and explain why you prefer certain days.
advanced.modelAnswer: Le lundi matin, j'ai un rendez-vous important. L'après-midi, je travaille au bureau. Le mercredi, c'est mon jour préféré parce que je finis tôt. Le vendredi soir, je sors avec mes amis. Le samedi et le dimanche, j'aime rester à la maison et me reposer.
advanced.modelAnswerExplanation: This response uses detailed time markers ('le matin,' 'l'après-midi,' 'le soir'), distinguishes between habitual and specific times, and provides reasons for preferences using 'parce que.'
advanced.tip: Structure your response with time markers and use connectors like 'parce que' and 'mais' to explain preferences. Combine days with time periods for more natural speech.
